text:
Matt Coronato is the kind of player the numbers argue about. He has 16 points in 22 games for Calgary, seven of them on the power play, after 45 in 80 games last season. Corey Sznajder's All Three Zones tracking loved his offense in 2025-26: 8.5 scoring chances per 60 from in front of the net (98th percentile among forwards) and 9.6 primary shot assists per 60 (93rd).

Evolving-Hockey saw the other end. It had him around replacement level last season, -1.7 wins, mostly because opponents got far more chances with him on the ice, bottom 1% of forwards. That hasn't fixed itself: the Flames have 45% of the expected goals with him at five on five, worse than without him.

The recent stretch is cooler, six points in ten against 7.5 we'd expect at his ice time, and his own chances are down a touch from last year. His shooting (10.6%) is a little under his normal, so the goals should come at about the rate they have. What decides his value is whether the play stops tilting the wrong way when he's out there.
